source.title: Downside Market Risk: A Key Determinant of Cryptocurrency Returns
source.author: Aleksandr Kusliaikin

hypothesis: Cryptocurrencies with higher causal downside beta to the contemporaneous crypto market earn higher subsequent weekly returns as compensation for crash-state exposure.
universe: Point-in-time Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals. Each Monday retain the top 50 by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume among assets with exact daily history and sufficient downside-market observations.
market_proxy: Equal-weight daily return across all contemporaneously available Binance perpetuals with valid daily returns; no future constituent list is used.
feature: Downside beta estimated over prior completed UTC days only: cov(asset return, market return | market return < 0) / var(market return | market return < 0). Require at least max(5, floor(W/5)) valid downside observations.
signal_direction: Positive risk premium: long highest downside-beta quintile, short lowest downside-beta quintile.
portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral long/short, 0.5 gross per side.
execution: Feature and liquidity inputs end Sunday 23:59 UTC; rebalance Monday 00:00 UTC open and hold to next Monday open.
development_gate: Canonical rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive high-minus-low beta spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 windows positive after base costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; canonical OOS rank IC >0.02; positive at 2x costs; at least 2/3 windows positive; 2024 and 2025 each non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; DSR reported.
source_deviation: The source studies rolling downside-risk betas on weekly cryptocurrency data. This adaptation uses daily returns derived causally from 1h Binance perpetual OHLCV, a point-in-time liquidity universe, and an equal-weight market proxy because historical point-in-time market capitalization is unavailable.
